name: hardwood
summary: Interior joinery: a carved bookcase, a tavern table, a chair back. Wood that has been indoors and worked.
why: The third wood in the library and the one with the clearest case for existing. wood is a
turned weapon haft, oiled by a hand and argued down to 0.08 of depth. timber is a sawn post
left in the rain at 0.82 roughness. This is neither: it is joinery, planed and carved and
kept dry, and MU draws it as dark oak with deep scrollwork cut into it.
Roughness 0.58, by a distance the smoothest wood here. Furniture indoors is waxed and
handled and never weathered, so it holds a broad soft highlight - which is most of what
separates a table from a fence post at a glance.
Depth 0.30, against timber's 0.15. The relief here is real and it is the point: bookshelf
and desk_big are photographs of carved panels, and the dark in them is a chisel cut rather
than a stain. This is the opposite case to plaster, where the dark was dirt on a flat wall.
Brushed along v. Planed board has its grain running the length of the piece and indoor wood
is the one place that grain is close enough to be seen.
